legal_status_notes: CRITICAL EXEMPTION RULE FOR MAHARASHTRA: Section 3(1)(b) excludes banks, PSUs, multinational corporations, and companies with paid-up capital of ₹1 Crore or more. Such corporate tenancies fall under TPA 1882.

section_or_rule_title: Landlord's right to recover possession of premises given on licence on expiry
chapter_or_part: Chapter VII: Summary Disposal of Certain Applications
exact_text:
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, a licensee in possession or occupation of premises given to him on licence for residence shall deliver possession of such premises to the landlord on expiry of the period of licence; and on the failure of the licensee to so deliver the possession of the licensed premises, a landlord shall be entitled to recover possession of such premises from a licensee, on the expiry of the period of licence, by making an application to the Competent Authority, and the Competent Authority, on being satisfied that the period of licence has expired, shall pass an order for eviction of a licensee.
(2) Any licensee who does not deliver possession of the premises to the landlord on expiry of the period of licence and continues to be in possession of the licensed premises till he is dispossessed by the Competent Authority shall be liable to pay damages at double the rate of the licence fee or charge of the premises fixed under the agreement of licence.
(3) The Competent Authority shall not entertain any claim of whatever nature from any other person who is not a licensee according to the agreement of licence.
Explanation.—For the purposes of this section,—
(a) the expression 'landlord' includes a successor-in-interest who becomes the landlord of the premises by reason of death of such landlord or otherwise;
(b) an agreement of licence in writing shall be conclusive evidence of the fact stated therein.
legal_status_notes: CRITICAL LEAVE & LICENSE RECOVERY: Fast-track summary eviction before the Competent Authority. Licensee overstaying after expiry must pay DOUBLE THE LICENSE FEE as statutory damages.

section_or_rule_title: Tenancy agreement to be compulsorily registered
exact_text:
(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, any agreement for a licence or letting of any premises, entered into between the landlord and the tenant or the licensee, as the case may be, after the commencement of this Act, shall be in writing and shall be registered under the Registration Act, 1908.
(2) The responsibility of getting such agreement registered shall be on the landlord and in the absence of the written registered agreement, the contention of the tenant about the terms and conditions, subject to which a premises have been given on licence or let to him by the landlord, shall prevail, unless proved otherwise.
(3) Any landlord who contravenes the provisions of this section shall, on conviction, be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three months or with fine not exceeding rupees five thousand or with both.
legal_status_notes: CRUCIAL STATUTORY MANDATE: Every rental/leave and license agreement in Maharashtra MUST be in writing and registered. Landlord is legally responsible for registration; failure flips the burden of proof (tenant's word prevails) and subjects landlord to criminal conviction (up to 3 months imprisonment or ₹5,000 fine).
